html:
The Armenian revolution of 2018 was a peaceful protest movement in April and May 2018 that forced Serzh Sargsyan, who had moved from president to prime minister to stay in power, to resign.

The opposition MP Nikol Pashinyan walked from Gyumri to Yerevan and led weeks of street protests and civil disobedience. Sargsyan resigned on 23 April, saying "Nikol was right". Parliament elected Pashinyan prime minister on 8 May, and his alliance won elections later that year. He promised to fight corruption. The defeat in the war of 2020 and the loss of Karabakh in 2023 then dominated his rule, as Armenia drifted away from Russia.
sum: The Armenian revolution of 2018 was a peaceful protest movement in April and May 2018 that forced Serzh Sargsyan, who had moved from president to prime minister to stay in power, to resign.
